why: A (universes 0): for any Mathlib CovariantDerivative on the tangent bundle of any manifold (any model I), Milnor's rules (3) (cov Y x (f x • X x) = f x • cov Y x (X x)), additivity in Y and the Leibniz rule (4) at points where Y, f are differentiable. B: for manifolds modelled on ℝⁿ, (i) the pointwise rules, (ii) the global rules (1)-(4) for a smooth connection, and (iii) the converse: every operation D on smooth fields obeying (1)-(4) is the ⊢ of some smooth Mathlib connection. A_to_B_rules (in the .lean) proves (i)+(ii) from A (smoothness (1) from IsGlobalConn via Mathlib's ContMDiff.clm_bundle_apply). The missing part is (iii), 'rules (1)-(4) may serve as the definition': it needs locality of D (bump functions), extraction of Christoffel symbols in charts and patching them into a Mathlib CovariantDerivative defined on all sections — a construction the project does not have (Connection.lean says Christoffel symbols are not formalized). B ⇒ A holds only because A is provable outright from Mathlib's CovariantDerivative axioms (A is about arbitrary models I, which B does not cover); that direction is vacuous.
B_issue: B assumes neither Hausdorffness nor second countability; clause (iii) (locality of D via smooth bump functions) is standardly proved for Hausdorff manifolds, so its truth in B's generality is plausible but not certain.
overlap: B_to_A: 0 shared project theorems (A re-proved from Mathlib's IsCovariantDerivativeOn.add/leibniz)
